concepts.def: Open system: inputs (precipitation), outputs (evapotranspiration, discharge), stores (groundwater, vegetation).
Reservoirs storing more carbon than released: oceans (38,000 GtC), fossil fuels, terrestrial vegetation, soils.
Charles Keeling's continuous CO2 measurement from Mauna Loa since 1958; rose from 315 to 420+ ppm.
Arctic permafrost contains 1,500 GtC; thawing releases methane (28x more potent than CO2) creating feedback loop.
High evapotranspiration generates 50% of regional rainfall; deforestation reduces moisture recycling, prolongs droughts.
pH dropped 0.1 since pre-industrial as oceans absorb 30% of anthropogenic CO2; threatens coral reefs and shellfish.
